# node_modules

This directory is where the website's Node dependencies live. It is
**intentionally empty in version control** — everything under it is generated,
platform-specific, and reproducible from `package.json` and `package-lock.json`.

Only this README is tracked. Do not commit installed packages.

## Restoring the dependencies

From the repository root:

```powershell
npm install --prefix website
```

Or from inside `website/`:

```powershell
npm install
```

`npm install` reads `website/package-lock.json` and repopulates this directory
with the exact dependency versions the project was locked to. The install is
safe to repeat and safe to delete: removing `node_modules/` entirely and
re-running `npm install` always yields the same tree.

## Running the website after installing

```powershell
npm run dev --prefix website
```

The dev server is Vite. The site itself is static HTML, CSS, and vanilla
JavaScript — no framework runtime ships to the browser, so these dependencies
are build-time only.

Other available scripts:

- `npm run build --prefix website` — produce the static bundle in `website/dist/`
- `npm run preview --prefix website` — serve the built bundle locally

## Why this directory is not committed

A `node_modules/` tree is large, contains compiled binaries specific to one
operating system and CPU architecture, and changes on every dependency update.
Committing it bloats the repository and produces unusable files for anyone on a
different platform. The lockfile is the source of truth instead.
